b:
Moonlight like daylight

My mother came in my dream

A sad song from a film that Sowcar Janaki directed and starred in

In every line runs the sorrow of a daughter who has lost her mother. The eyes that carried that sorrow across the screen are now in eternal sleep

I haven't seen that Sowcar film. The film that introduced her to me was Iru Kodugal. Two wives fighting over one husband. The husband is a clerk while the wife is the Collector. She brings all this confusion before our eyes on the screen. With tear-filled eyes behind dark glasses, that same Janaki was in a lively role in Bama Vijayam. Suspecting Major Sundarrajan, setting off the family quarrel: her part enriched the story

Having shone in so many black-and-white films like this, her colour-film epic of fame was Puthiya Paravai. The song "Paartha Nyabagam Illaiyo", in which she acted to Susheela's voice as a woman infatuated with the West, is the peak of her career

Another appearance, in a character role in Thillu Mullu, with the same bounce as in the song "Varavu Ettana", undiminished.

I think she stayed away from cinema in the modern age. Only later did I learn that she had come to act as a heroine with a baby in her arms. A gem from Andhra who saw more than five generations in her own life

(In the song, a mother who has died sings to her daughter from the sky, blessing her and promising that if she is born again they will be together.)

If she is born again, she must come back to the screen

Today, let that gem sleep
note: Sowcar Janaki was a celebrated actress of Tamil and Telugu cinema. Iru Kodugal, Bama Vijayam, Puthiya Paravai and Thillu Mullu are films of hers; P. Susheela was the playback singer whose voice she acted to. A Collector is a senior district administrator in India.
